evidence: src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts: cancel() contains `if (body.reason.trim().length < 3) { throw new SubscriptionError('invalid', 'Give a cancellation reason'); }`, a business invariant on cancellation reasons.
The check throws a domain-layer error (SubscriptionError from src/domain/errors), which shows it is a domain rule enforced in an infrastructure adapter.
create() and resize() only delegate to use cases, which is the expected controller role, so `cancel` is the only misplaced responsibility.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This file is an HTTP controller in the infrastructure layer. Its job should be to map transport bodies to use-case calls and pass results back. `create` and `resize` do exactly that. `cancel` also enforces a business rule: a cancellation must have a reason of at least 3 non-whitespace characters, otherwise it throws the domain `SubscriptionError('invalid', 'Give a cancellation reason')`.

This is not transport-shape validation such as type or presence checks. It is an invariant on the subscription-cancellation workflow, and the fact that it throws a domain error shows it is a domain rule. Because it lives in the controller, any other caller of the `CancelSubscription` use case (CLI, job, another adapter) skips it. The rule should live in the domain (Subscription aggregate or a CancellationReason value object) or in the `CancelSubscription` application use case.
